newsitem.title: USA: Navajo Ariz. coal-fired unit start delayed to Mon.
newsitem.headline: Navajo Ariz. coal-fired unit start delayed to Mon.

text.p: Maintenance work on the 720 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Page, Ariz., has been extended to Monday, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Tuesday.
The unit was shut November 9 for work scheduled to finish Thursday, but the outage was extended because of turbine bearing problems, they said.
The Navajo plant's other two 720 MW units are said to be operating at normal rates.
The project's operator and 27-percent owner is Salt River Project, a public power agency in Phoenix. Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation and various public power companies.
